comparisons.peer_topic: Income Tax Expense Drivers and Effective Tax Rates
comparisons.peer_summary: The effective tax rates for 2024 and 2023 were primarily driven by recurring tax preference benefits from affordable housing and renewable energy investments; without these credits and discrete benefits, the rates would have been approximately 25 percent. The 2023 rate also included tax impacts related to the FDIC special assessment and BSBY cessation.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America disclose the primary drivers of their 2024 effective tax rates, but they cite different underlying causes. JPMorgan attributes its rate increase primarily to a new accounting adoption for tax credit structures and a specific charitable contribution of Visa shares. In contrast, Bank of America attributes its rate stability (absent discrete items) to recurring tax preference benefits from affordable housing and renewable energy investments, noting that without these credits and discrete benefits, the rate would have been approximately 25 percent, and highlighting specific 2023 impacts like FDIC assessments and BSBY cessation rather than the accounting change seen at JPM.

sentences.text: The effective tax rate increased predominantly driven by:

• a higher level of pretax income and changes in the mix of income and expenses subject to U.S. federal, state and local taxes, including the impact of the net gain on Visa shares and the contribution of Visa shares to the JPMorgan Chase Foundation recorded in the second quarter of 2024.

The effective tax rates for 2024 and 2023 were primarily driven by our recurring tax preference benefits, which primarily consisted of tax credits from investments in affordable housing and renewable energy.
Absent the tax credits and discrete tax benefits, the effective tax rates would have been approximately 25 percent for both periods.

comparisons.peer_summary: The effective tax rate was 25% in 2024 versus 27% in the prior year, largely driven by the geographic mix of earnings.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan Chase and Citigroup discuss the drivers of their effective tax rates in 2024, but report opposite trends and different primary drivers. JPMorgan reported an increased effective tax rate driven by a new accounting standard for tax credit structures and the mix of income including a Visa share contribution. Citigroup, however, reported a decreased effective tax rate to 25% (from 27% in the prior year), which it attributes largely to the geographic mix of earnings, without mentioning the specific tax credit structure accounting change or Visa-specific items that impacted JPMorgan.

comparisons.peer_summary: The effective income tax rate increased to 22.4% in 2024 from 20.7% in 2023, primarily driven by a decrease in the impact of permanent tax benefits, partially offset by changes in the geographic mix of earnings.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan Chase and Goldman Sachs disclose that their effective tax rates increased in 2024 compared to 2023, but they identify different primary drivers. JPMorgan attributes the increase to the adoption of updated Accounting for Investments in Tax Credit Structures guidance and higher pretax income/mix effects including Visa share transactions. Goldman Sachs attributes its increase (from 20.7% to 22.4%) primarily to a decrease in the impact of permanent tax benefits, partially offset by changes in the geographic mix of earnings, without mentioning the specific tax credit structure accounting update adopted by JPMorgan.

sentences.text: The effective tax rate increased predominantly driven by:

• a higher level of pretax income and changes in the mix of income and expenses subject to U.S. federal, state and local taxes, including the impact of the net gain on Visa shares and the contribution of Visa shares to the JPMorgan Chase Foundation recorded in the second quarter of 2024.

The effective income tax rate for 2024 was 22.4%, up from the full year income tax rate of 20.7% for 2023, primarily due to a decrease in the impact of permanent tax benefits for 2024 compared with 2023, partially offset by changes in the geographic mix of earnings.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company is evaluating an update enhancing income tax disclosures, including disaggregation of income tax rate reconciliations and taxes paid, effective for annual periods beginning January 1, 2025; no material impact is expected.
comparisons.comparison: While JPMorgan Chase discloses a specific accounting change (Accounting for Investments in Tax Credit Structures) that impacted its 2024 effective tax rate, Morgan Stanley discloses an upcoming accounting update for income tax disclosures effective in 2025 regarding the disaggregation of rate reconciliations. Neither company cites the other's specific tax credit structure accounting adoption, and MS's disclosure concerns future reporting requirements for rate reconciliation rather than the drivers of the 2024 effective tax rate itself.

sentences.text: The effective tax rate increased predominantly driven by:

• Income Tax Disclosures. This update enhances annual income tax disclosures primarily to further disaggregate disclosures related to the income tax rate reconciliation and income taxes paid. For the income tax rate reconciliation, this update requires (1) disclosure of specific categories of reconciling items (where applicable), and (2) providing additional information for reconciling items that meet a quantitative threshold. For income taxes paid (net of refunds), this update requires disclosure of amounts disaggregated by (1) federal, state, and foreign taxes; and (2) individual jurisdictions that meet a quantitative threshold. Additionally, the update requires disclosure of (1) income (or loss) before income taxes, disaggregated between domestic and foreign; and (2) income tax expense disaggregated by federal, state and foreign. The update is effective for annual periods beginning January 1, 2025, with early adoption permitted.
